summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for elective banding of her left brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula due to steal syndrome causing hand pain, numbness, and poor perfusion. After initial banding failed to resolve symptoms, a fistulagram confirmed ongoing steal, leading to a revision surgery involving cephalic vein harvest and reconfiguration of flow from the radial artery. Postoperatively, her symptoms resolved, radial pulse returned, and she tolerated full-dose dialysis without issues. Anticoagulation was managed with heparin drip during warfarin hold, then transitioned back to warfarin as INR reached therapeutic levels. She was discharged home in stable condition with detailed instructions on access site care, anticoagulation management, and when to seek urgent care.
